app.name: A11yTextHelper
help.step_1_body: Results appear as you type. Currently focusing on Web issues. Try +required -excluded to narrow results (e.g. keyboard +screen reader -wcag2.2). These options can be changed in Settings.
help.step_2_body: Prioritize results up or down to change their ranking. Starred results always appear first. Pin any result to keep it visible at the top across all searches.
help.step_3_body: Select the finding that best matches. Results are ranked by relevance.
help.step_4_body: Add a location prefix (e.g. "Global:") or use AI Assist to revise the wording. Describe what you observed and the AI will tailor the finding to your context.
help.step_5_body: Copy the description and remediation steps directly into your spreadsheet or report. Use Copy All to grab both fields at once.
help.shortcuts_note: Shortcuts are only active when focus is on the result list. Use them to quickly navigate and rate findings without leaving the list.
help.take_tour_description: See an interactive walkthrough of how to search, prioritize, and export findings.
onboarding.heading: Welcome to A11yTextHelper
onboarding.confirm_body: You have not reached the end of the tour. Close now and skip the rest?
onboarding.slide_1_body: Search by symptom, WCAG success criterion, or component name. Filter by platform (Web or Native) and WCAG level. Use Narrow Results to search within what is already showing. Results are sorted by severity.
onboarding.slide_2_body: Star a finding and it will always appear at the top of results, above anything upvoted. Upvote or downvote to tune the rank order below that. Pin a finding to keep it visible at the top regardless of what you search for.
onboarding.slide_3_body: Open a finding to see the title, WCAG success criterion, description, and remediation steps. Add a location note to the description (e.g. "Global:"), use AI Assist to revise any field, then copy each field individually or use Copy All to grab everything at once.
about.what_body: This is your manual accessibility audit writing assistant. If you've done a few, you've done them all. Mostly. If you've been doing this a while you know how often we run into the same accessibility issues over and over again. I wanted to save myself the time of having to dig into old files and reports to find near-identical issues from past accessibility audits.
about.what_body_2: Consistency is key, especially in this industry and I wanted to make sure I was consistent with impact, severity, descriptions, and the oft-times similar suggested technical remediation steps. Search this homebrew library of WCAG-aligned finding write-ups, pick one that matches your observation, customize or add specifics to it, and copy/paste it straight into your audit report.
about.what_wcag: This data extends up to {wcag} (Level A and AA).
about.step_1_body: Type what you observed — a component name, element type, or plain-language description.
about.step_2_body: Use the Priority Up/Priority Down arrows on each result to tune how results are ranked. Star to show first. Archive to hide. Pin any result to keep it visible at the top across all searches.
about.step_3_body: Select the finding that best matches. Results are ranked by relevance.
about.step_4_body: Add a location prefix (e.g. "Global:") or use AI Assist to revise the wording — describe what you observed and the AI will tailor the finding to your context.
about.step_5_body: Copy the description and remediation steps directly into your spreadsheet or report. Use Copy All to grab both fields at once.
about.feature_ai_body: Refine any finding description with a short note. Your API key, your AI provider — never stored server-side.
about.feature_languages_body: The UI is available in over 50 languages including RTL support. Switch in Settings.
about.feature_party_body: It's in Settings. Under Appearance. You'll know it when you see it.
about.feature_pinning_body: Pin any finding to keep it at the top across all searches and views. Use the priority arrows to rank others, star to float a finding to the very top, or archive to remove it from view.
about.feature_a11y_body: Built to WCAG 2.2: focus management, live regions, keyboard navigation, reduced motion support, and high-contrast tokens.
about.sources_body: Entries are written in plain language, near-duplicates are consolidated, and each is aligned to a specific WCAG success criterion. Sources consulted include:
about.coming_auth: Optional sign-in with Google or GitHub to sync your settings across devices.
about.coming_custom: Add and edit your own custom findings, stored privately in the cloud.
about.coming_ai: Additional AI providers: OpenAI, Google Gemini, and more.

settings.ai_enable_desc: Rewrites text based on your refinement notes.
settings.privacy_body_1: API keys are stored locally in your browser (localStorage) and sent only to the AI provider's own API — never to any intermediate server. You can clear them at any time by removing the key and saving, or by clearing your browser's site data.
settings.privacy_body_2: This app stores the following in your browser: your theme preference, your language preference, your platform filter (Web/Native), your live search setting, your active AI provider, one API key per provider you configure, your finding priority data (priorities, stars, and archived items), your pinned findings, a list of recently viewed finding IDs (localStorage), any findings you create or copy (localStorage), and the ID of the last finding you had open (sessionStorage — cleared when the tab closes). No other data is stored or transmitted.
settings.privacy_body_translations: UI translations and base public corpus translations were generated with AI and may contain errors or missing data. No custom or user-entered data is ever sent out for translation.
settings.api_key_error: Error: API key is required when AI Assist is enabled.
settings.agentic_mode_desc: AI will search your corpus to match your style and technical depth when rewriting.
